This is the name assigned to the device. Each device logged in on a Warren account gets a unique name that helps you identify it when you manage your devices in the app or on the website.
You can have up to 5 devices logged in on one Warren account.
If you log out, the device and the device name is removed. When you log back in again, the device will get a new name.
The Auto-connect and Lockdown mode settings can be found in the Android system settings, follow this guide to enable one or both.
1. After clicking on the \"Go to VPN settings\" button below, click on the cogwheel next to the \"Warren VPN\" name.
Auto-connect is called Always-on VPN in the Android system settings and it makes sure you are constantly connected to the VPN tunnel and auto connects after restart.
2. To enable Auto-connect, click on the toggle next to \"Always-on VPN\".
The Lockdown mode is called \"Block connections without VPN\" in the Android system settings. It helps minimize leaks, however it has some known limitations which you can read more about

3. To enable Lockdown mode, click on the toggle next to \"Block connections without VPN\".

To make sure that you have the most secure version and to inform you of any issues with the current version that is running, the app performs version checks automatically. This sends the app version and Android system version to Warren servers. Warren keeps counters on number of used app versions and Android versions. The data is never stored or used in any way that can identify you.

If the split tunneling feature is used, then the app queries your system for a list of all installed applications. This list is only retrieved in the split tunneling view. The list of installed applications is never sent from the device.
